BRINGING OUT 
THE BEST IN US 


2015 Community Report 


y 5 @) Pinter 2 


| 
' 


Not everyone gets a chance to learn, grow and thrive in a welcoming and positive social 
environment. That’s why we offer financial assistance to those who need it most. 


As a charitable organization and a social enterprise, we invest in activities and services that 
meet the needs of the community and that are accessible to as many people as possible. 
Your support is vital to delivering these initiatives to the communities we serve. 


By supporting the YMCA, you are providing opportunities for kids, young people and families 
to be the best they can be. You are helping build a stronger community. One that is more active, 


inclusive and engaged. 


Here are the stories of Jirer, the Meflah family and Alexander, just some of the thousands of 
people we are helping thanks to your generosity. 


/ 


Catherine Isabelle 
Chair of the Board of Directors 
The YMCAs of Québec 


ns ae 


Gregory Chrispin Stéphane Vaillancourt 
President President and CEO 
The YMCAs of Québec Foundation The YMCAs of Québec 


Unhealthy lifestyle habits have become public enemy 
number One. Excessive weight, obesity, chronic disease... 
Physical inactivity now kills as many people as smoking! 

f 


Only 9% of young people aged 5 to 17 get at least 60 
minutes of physical activity per day. As our children learn 
to read and write, they should learn to be active! 


We need to get them moving as early as possible, in day 
care and at school, during recreational and extracurricular 
activities, in after-school programs, at camp and in Youth 
Zones. Not only do exercise and sports allow kids to 
channel their energy and socialize with their peers, 

but they also help children focus and learn. 


“When | come here, 
| learn. Not just 
about basketball. 

| learn about life 
and | succeed 

at school.” 


Jirer 


Meee ent rege Your generosity and the support of companies such as CN, Caisse populaire 
Desjardins des Versants du Mont-Royal, Mamie Clafoutis Inc. and Ubisoft 
Divertissements Inc. make it possible for the YMCA to give everyone the 
opportunity to lead a healthy and active life, regardless of age, income 
or physical ability.

y 


If you met the Meflah children, 
you would find it hard to believe 
that they couldn't speak French 
twelve months ago when they 
came to Canada from Algeria. 


Their parents, Salim and Sinsabel, 
were worried about the problems 
the kids were having at school. 
They couldn't give them individual 
attention with their homework. 
So, they signed their kids up to the 
Y's homework help program. 


What a relief! They made fast 
progress; they learned French, got 
better grades, made new friends... 


It was more than just homework 
help. It was a way for the whole 
family to integrate into their 
new country. 


A better future for 2,00 youth in our communities 


“It was important for us to be associated with an organization that is recognized across the 
province for its work with young people. The YMCAs of Québec’s history, impact and strong 
presence within the community makes them a partner of choice.” 

David Nish, Chief Executive of Standard Life 


Standard Life’s generous donation of $750,000 will give our Youth Zone participants an 
opportunity to learn how to make good choices, resist peer pressure, resolve conflicts, 
make friends, interact with other cultures, gain self-confidence and acquire solid values 
from positive adult role models in a safe and healthy environment. 


The YMCA Peace Medals raised $205,000 


“Itis an honour to work with the YMCA in honouring those who work to make our society 
more peaceful and harmonious. The success of the Peace Medal event has shown me that 
Quebecers truly do share in these values. This sets the stage for a better future for our children. 
Brian Bronfman, President, Peace Grantmakers Network 


” 


Thousands of young people will continue to enjoy YMCA community programs that help 
them develop their social, leadership and conflict resolution skills. For an unforgettable 
evening, many thanks to our presenter, Manulife, and to our sponsors: the Brian Bronfman 
Foundation, GDI Services (Québec) SEC, lvanhoé Cambridge, Servicorp, Telus, Borden 
Ladner Gervais LLP and the Peace Grantmakers Network. 


Many thanks to: 


Corus Entertainment Inc., the Céline and Jacques Lamarre Foundation, the Claude Beaulieu Foundation, 
Fondation de la Pointe-de-I’lle, the La Capitale Financial Group Foundation, the Organix Foundation, 
the Medavie Health Foundation, Fondation Québec Jeunes, KPMG LLP, Réno-Meétrix and 

SNC-Lavalin Inc. We are also very grateful to the late Alfred Fred Muth and William Ridley for their legacy 
gifts, which will help us accomplish our mission for decades to come.

At a time when social harmony is under constant threat, it is more important than ever to work 
towards a fair, inclusive, empathetic, safe and respectful society for people of all backgrounds. 
Reaching out to different communities is one of the YMCA’s core values. 


At the Y, we do everything we can to create a more positive and inclusive environment in which 
everyone is respected and valued. We help people cultivate healthy relationships and encourage 
better communication. We also offer a welcoming support network where people can find the 
encouragement and tools they need to achieve their personal goals, no matter their age, origin, 
ability or income.

“If he hadn't been 
able to come here, 
he would have never 
known how good it 
feels to have friends.” 


Monique, 
Alexander's mother 


By making our services 
easier to access and 

by fostering an inclusive 
environment, YOU are 
creating a more harmonious 
society and helping our 
community members feel 
like they really belong. 


Loneliness, depression, 
isolation... this is what could 
lie ahead for Alexander, a 
10-year-old kid with autism. 


Making contacts. Creating 
friendships. Feeling accepted. 
Being himself. This is what 


matters most to his mother 
who signed him up for the 
YMCA's day camp and 
after-school program. 


Now, everybody in the 
neighbourhood knows 
Alexander. His mother is 
relieved to see that he is 
part of acommunity that 
he can connect to. 


A special thanks to donors who share our vision, such as the George Hogg 
Family Foundation, the Caisse Populaire Desjardins de Bois-Franc — Cartierville, 
the Echo Foundation and the Cowan Foundation.
